name: Bielefeld
assessment: The official municipal Amt für Geoinformation und Kataster is evidenced as the Bielefeld cadastral custodian. Its official open-data ALKIS parcel WFS returned a bounded anonymous parcel response with native IDs and geometry. Runtime remains held pending serial review.
queryAndRequestOutcome: Separate English and German discovery was performed. Municipal Geoportal, cadastral-office, service-portal, and open-data pages were found. WFS GetCapabilities returned HTTP 200 XML. A WFS 1.1.0 GetFeature request in EPSG:25832 over a bounded area containing the exact WUP point returned HTTP 200 CSV with 279 records. Only three full polygons were retained.

schemaAndCrs.viewerConfig: Official open-data dataset links to the WFS capabilities endpoint.

retainedSamples.propertiesShape: exactly one canonical native identity: {id: native WFS id}

attempts.outcome: Municipal cadastral custodian and ALKIS scope verified.
Official ALKIS parcel-area dataset and WFS link retrieved.
279 bounded parcel rows returned with native id and WKT geometry; response was not treated as citywide proof.

scopeLimits: Exact WUP point preserved and not shifted.
Bounded sample area includes the WUP point but no exact-point membership claim is made.
No citywide completeness or exact-point absence inference.
No raw source-specific attribute set retained beyond ignored scratch CSV.
This is research evidence, not source integration/admission.

qualification.reason: Public parcel geometry is verified, but adapter qualification, CRS/axis conventions, WFS limit semantics, identity admission, and citywide coverage remain for serial review.

uncertainty: The official municipal service is openly queryable and returned safe ID-plus-geometry records. The WFS response included additional source fields that were observed but not retained. The service’s exact pagination/limit behavior and citywide completeness were not established. No login, credential, private token, CAPTCHA bypass, unsafe field request, or TLS disablement was used.
